# Time to do something about reproducibility

## Authors

- Sean J Morrison<sup>1</sup> †

### Affiliations

1. Sean J Morrison is an Investigator of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute, and Director of the Children’s Research Institute at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center Dallas USA . He is also the Mary McDermott Cook Chair in Pediatric Genetics and Director of the Hamon Laboratory for Stem Cells and Cancer at UTSW, and a Cancer Prevention and Research Institute of Texas Scholar sean.morrison@utsouthwestern.edu

† Corresponding author

## Abstract

Individual scientists, scientific communities and scientific journals can do more to assess the publication of irreproducible results, to promote good science, and to increase the efficiency with which the scientific community self-corrects.

results.result: Individual scientists, scientific communities, and scientific journals can do more to assess the publication of irreproducible results.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3 are normative statements presented without supporting data, empirical evidence, or citations. All three claims are marked as speculation with no experimental or analytical basis provided in the manuscript excerpt.

results.result: Individual scientists, scientific communities, and scientific journals can do more to promote good science.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C6 are normative assertions without supporting evidence, data, or citations. These claims are speculative and lack empirical validation or concrete examples demonstrating how these stakeholders could promote good science.

results.result: Individual scientists, scientific communities, and scientific journals can increase the efficiency of the scientific community's self-correction mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C7-C9 are normative statements without supporting evidence. While C10 correctly infers that a self-correction mechanism exists (a generally accepted concept), no data or analysis is provided to support that these stakeholders can increase its efficiency.
